question_text: If the mean and variance of a binomial variable X are 2.4 and 1.44 respectively, then find P(1 < X ≤ 4).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find P(1 < X ≤ 4) from the mean and variance — how you get q, p and n, and which three terms you add.
insider_note: Variance over mean gives q, not p — 1.44/2.4 = 3/5 — and the fractions should be fifths from the start, since every power later is over 5; 1 < X ≤ 4 keeps exactly three terms, X = 2, 3 and 4.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find n, p, q
steps.margin_note: First mark. Divide variance by mean: q = 1.44/2.4 = 0.6 = 3/5, so p = 2/5, and n = 2.4/(2/5) = 6. Convert to fifths at once — the powers in the next step are all over 5.

recall.must_convey: That npq/np gives q = 3/5, so p = 2/5 and n = 6.
accept: divide the variance by the mean to get q three by five, then p is two by five and n is six
one point four four by two point four is point six so q is three fifths and n is six

steps.why: The two given numbers are two equations in n and p; dividing removes n and gives q. Converting 0.6 to 3/5 before substituting keeps every power a clean fraction.
common_mistakes: Keeping q = 0.6 and p = 0.4 as decimals and then raising decimals to powers.

steps.label: Find P(1 < X ≤ 4)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 1 < X ≤ 4 keeps X = 2, 3, 4 — three terms. Each is ⁶Cᵣ (3/5)⁶⁻ʳ (2/5)ʳ; put everything over 5⁶ = 15625: 15·81·4 + 20·27·8 + 15·9·16 = 4860 + 4320 + 2160 = 11340. Reduce by 5 to 2268/3125.

accept: P of one less than X less than or equal to four is P of two plus P of three plus P of four, all over five to the six, which is eleven thousand three forty by fifteen thousand six twenty five equals two two six eight by three one two five

steps.why: The event is three values of X, so the probability is three terms of the same formula. Writing all three over the common denominator 5⁶ turns the sum into whole-number arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Including X = 1 or leaving out X = 4.
